claims.claim: A Node service reading a precomputed table is far inside the [300 ms] budget
claims.measured: Single-row Postgres query, 64 connections: node-express p50 6.66 ms, p99 17.28 ms; node-fastify p50 6.40 ms, p99 14.54 ms
claims.why: Measured Node latency for one indexed DB read is about 15–20 ms at p99, far below 300 ms.

claims.claim: Serving a precomputed top-50 list is a single-digit-millisecond read
claims.about: TypeScript/Node service doing one indexed Postgres lookup
claims.measured: Single-row Postgres query p50: node-express 6.66 ms, node-fastify 6.40 ms, bun-elysia 1.94 ms, deno-hono 3.36 ms (p99 4–17 ms)
claims.why: Median latency for one DB read on the TypeScript/Node stacks is 2–7 ms, and p99 is within about 2x of single digits.

claims.claim: The 300 ms budget depends on query shape, precomputation, and caching, not on the language
claims.about: Language choice for a single-lookup endpoint (TypeScript vs Go etc.)
claims.measured: Single-row Postgres p99: node-fastify 14.54 ms, go-gin 6.00 ms, bun-elysia 4.10 ms, rust-actix 6.70 ms; only php-laravel (p50 410 ms) exceeds 300 ms
claims.why: For the stacks being considered, the language gaps are a few to tens of milliseconds, which is small next to a 300 ms budget. Only non-Octane Laravel would miss it.

claims.claim: Go is a reasonable carve-out later if a ranking service becomes CPU-bound (implying Go beats Node on CPU-bound work)
claims.measured: CPU fib(20): go-gin 18,218 req/s, go-nethttp 15,093 vs node-express 7,213, node-fastify 8,308 (bun-elysia 18,041, deno-hono 14,144)
claims.why: Go measured about 2–2.5x Node on CPU-bound requests, which is the direction implied. Bun was about as fast as Go, though.
